text.en: Standing in the heart of the capital is a place where a flame burns day and night to remember brave people. This short poem takes you to that place, the National War Memorial in New Delhi.

The National War Memorial in New Delhi was established in February 2019. It is a national monument built by the Government of India in honour of our brave soldiers. The pictures show the memorial itself and Amar Jawan Jyoti, the eternal flame.
The poem describes the memorial as a grand sight in the heartland of Bharat, honouring brave stories that are told again and again. It stands with respect, grace and pride, and every name and stone carries a story. The soldiers are remembered from battlefields, skies and wide oceans, because they stood for Bharat side by side. The eternal flame glows in silence and pays homage to their courage. Their sacrifice is always in our minds, in blessed memory. The poem ends with a promise to remember with pride and respect the sacrifice of the soldiers at the memorial.
Read the poem aloud, recite it with your classmates and teacher, and try to remember it. Visit the website of the National War Memorial, given in the book as mygov.in, to learn more about it, and plan a visit with your teacher or parents.
This chapter's last page also holds the transcript for a listening task from Unit 5 about a dish called gakkad bharta, which a speaker from Jabalpur in Madhya Pradesh describes. Gakkad is made from wheat dough balls roasted on high heat. Bharta is made by roasting brinjals and tomatoes and garnishing with chopped onions, coriander, green chillies and salt. It is made without frying, and is eaten by crumbling gakkad, adding bharta and a spoonful of ghee.
Let us learn the important words of the poem. Heartland means the central part of a country or region, so the poem places the memorial at the centre of the nation. To etch is to carve a mark into a surface so it lasts. When the poem speaks of names that are etched, it means they are cut into the stone to stay for ever. Eternal means lasting for ever and never ending. Homage is respect shown openly to someone we honour, and a sacrifice is giving up something very precious, even life, for others. A poem is made for the ear as well as for meaning, so listen to its rhymes. Words at the ends of lines sound alike in pairs, such as the pair of words behold and retold, and the pair wide and side. This pattern, where two lines end with the same sound, makes the poem easy to say aloud and easy to remember. That is why the book asks you to recite it with your class. Notice the order of the poem too. It first describes the memorial, then the soldiers from land, sky and sea, then the glowing flame, and it ends with a promise to remember. Think about why the soldiers are remembered from battlefields, skies and oceans. Soldiers, airmen and sailors protect the country on land, in the air and on the sea. Now say in your own words why a memorial is built. It gives everyone a place to pause, to feel grateful and to remember those who gave their lives for the country. Finally, say how you can show respect when you visit such a place: stay quiet, stand with care, and think about the sacrifice that the place stands for.
The National War Memorial in New Delhi was established in February 2019.
It is a national monument built by the Government of India in honour of our brave soldiers who served the nation.
Look closely at the chapter pictures: they show the grand circular memorial complex itself and Amar Jawan Jyoti, the eternal flame.
The poem opens by calling the memorial a grand sight set in the heartland of Bharat, right in the capital city.
It honours brave stories of courage and duty that citizens tell again and again across generations.
The monument stands with quiet respect, grace and pride, and every carved name and stone carries a personal story of service.
Soldiers are remembered from battlefields on land, from high skies above, and from wide oceans around India's coasts.
The poem brings land, air and sea forces together to show that the Army, Air Force and Navy stood for Bharat side by side.

text.en: Then our attention turns to the eternal flame, which glows in solemn silence and pays homage to their fearless courage.
Their sacrifice is always in our minds, kept alive in blessed memory whenever citizens visit or think of their duty.
The poem ends with a promise: we will remember with pride and respect the sacrifice of our soldiers at the memorial.
Let us read the important words of the poem carefully so their meanings stay clear in our minds.
Heartland means the central part of a country or region, so placing the memorial in the heartland shows it belongs to the heart of Bharat.
To etch means to carve a mark into a hard surface so it lasts. Names etched in stone are cut to remain for ever.
Eternal means lasting for ever and never ending, just like the flame that burns day and night at the memorial.
Homage means deep respect shown openly in honour of someone, while sacrifice means giving up something very precious, even life, for others.
A poem is crafted for the ear as well as for meaning, so pay close attention to its rhyming line endings.
Words at the ends of lines sound alike in pairs, such as behold with retold, and wide with side.
This clear rhyming pattern gives the verse a steady rhythm, making it easy to recite aloud and easy to remember by heart.
Notice how the textbook asks you to read the poem aloud and recite it together with your classmates and teacher.
Follow the logical sequence of the poem too: first the grand memorial site, then the soldiers across land, sky and sea.
Next comes the silently glowing flame, and finally our shared promise to hold their sacrifice in lasting memory.
The textbook also points us to the official National War Memorial website on mygov.in to learn more facts and stories.
You are encouraged to plan a respectful visit to the memorial with your teacher or parents when you are in New Delhi.
The final page of this Unit 5 chapter also carries the transcript for a listening task about a regional dish called gakkad bharta.
The speaker describes this traditional food from Jabalpur in Madhya Pradesh, naming each ingredient clearly.
Gakkad is made from wheat dough balls roasted on high heat, while bharta is prepared by roasting brinjals and tomatoes with onion, coriander, green chillies and salt.
Notice that the dish is cooked without any frying, and it is eaten by crumbling hot gakkad, mixing in bharta, and adding a spoonful of ghee.
Think in your own words why a nation builds a memorial: it gives citizens a calm, shared place to pause and feel grateful.
When you visit such a memorial, show respect by walking quietly, standing with care, and reflecting on the courage it stands for.
